$comment: Storyboard for the 90-120 s booth video. record.mjs types each demo shot's phrase into the offline replay (src/renderer/dev/showcase-scenarios.js) verbatim, with [YOUR CLASS] filled from `presenter` as DEMO.md says ('say your real class'); narrate.mjs speaks each narration line; edit.mjs assembles title card, footage, closing card, badge and captions. Claims follow showcase/FACTS.md. The look is a red variant of showcase/DESIGN.md, as the presenter asked.
title: Ghost-Prime demo walkthrough

edit.$comment: edit.mjs knobs. Typing stretches over speedUpTypingOver seconds run at typingSpeed; idle stretches between shots over speedUpIdleOver seconds (nothing on screen changes) run at idleSpeed; answers always stream at 1x. lead/tail: seconds of footage kept before the first and after the last shot.

shots.narration: Ghost-Prime, by Ivan Lucky. Use a computer just by talking.

card.statement: Use a computer just by talking.

shots.narration: Ghost-Prime is an AI assistant on a school Chromebook. You talk or type, and it does the task.
shots.caption: Talk or type. It does the task.
shots.why: The answer streams in word by word with a CLAUDE tag. Inside 10 seconds the viewer knows what Ghost-Prime is.

shots.phrase: Go to the Wikipedia website, search for photosynthesis, and explain it to me in three simple sentences.
shots.narration: Now it reads the web for you. It opens Wikipedia, types the search itself, reads the article, and explains it in three simple sentences. Every step shows as a card.
shots.caption: Reads the web, explains it simply
shots.why: The hero demo used across the whole kit (DEMO.md Demo 5). Tool cards: browser_navigate, browser_get_page (numbered elements), browser_fill, screenshot, browser_get_text, then the three-sentence answer.

shots.phrase: Remember that I'm in [YOUR CLASS] and my favourite subject is chemistry.
shots.narration: It remembers you from one day to the next. Tell it something once; the memory is stored on the Chromebook.
shots.caption: It remembers what you tell it
shots.why: memory_save card, then 'Got it, I'll remember…'. The rehearsed phrase with the real class filled in (DEMO.md: say your real class). FACTS: memory WORKING; DEMO.md: 'the memories are stored on this Chromebook'.

shots.phrase: What do you know about me?
shots.narration: In a brand-new chat, it still knows: what you just said, and what it learned before.
shots.caption: A new chat. It still knows.
shots.why: Ctrl+N first (DEMO.md: ask in a chat that never heard it). memory_recall card, then the list including the memory just saved.

shots.phrase: Remind me in two minutes to drink some water.
shots.narration: Reminders, for homework and revision. Two minutes from now it speaks up, in the chat and out loud.
shots.caption: Reminders that speak up
shots.why: reminder_set card with the time. FACTS: reminders WORKING (desktop notification and spoken alert). The firing itself is not in the video.

shots.phrase: Make me a three-day chemistry revision plan and save it in a new folder called Showcase, so I can undo it if I change my mind.
shots.narration: Files too. It writes a three-day revision plan and saves it in a new folder. What it creates with its file tools can be undone.
shots.caption: Makes files, with undo
shots.why: file_create card with ~/Showcase/chemistry-revision-plan.txt. Also the setup for the PLAN demo: the folder now exists. FACTS: files with undo WORKING.

shots.narration: Safety for teachers. In plan mode it only looks: asked to delete that folder, it explains what it would do and changes nothing. An 'are you sure?' pop-up is next.
shots.caption: PLAN mode: it only looks
shots.why: /mode plan typed first (never Shift+Tab). A read-only Glob card, then 'I'm in PLAN mode, so I haven't changed anything…'. FACTS §5: PLAN is read-only, tested offline; no 'are you sure?' pop-up yet.

shots.narration: Recorded from the app's offline replay. Come and try it live at the booth.
